tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

---
# site.yml — provision and deploy the "ledger" Django app behind nginx
# Usage: ansible-playbook -i inventories/prod site.yml --tags deploy -e app_version=2.14.3

- name: Provision and deploy ledger application servers
  hosts: ledger_app
  become: true
  become_method: sudo
  gather_facts: true
  serial: "30%"
  vars_files:
    - vars/common.yml
    - "vars/{{ deploy_env | default('staging') }}.yml"
    - vault/secrets.yml   # encrypted with ansible-vault, see README
  vars:
    app_name: ledger
    app_user: ledger
    app_root: /srv/ledger
    app_port:   8081
    release_dir: "{{ app_root }}/releases/{{ app_version }}"
    app_users:
      - { name: ledger, uid: 1501, groups: [www-data] }
      - { name: ledger-ops, uid: 1502, groups: [adm, sudo] }
      - name: ledger-ci
        uid: 1503
        groups: []

  pre_tasks:
    - name: Refresh apt cache
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        update_cache: true
        cache_valid_time: 3600
      when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
      tags: [always]

    - name: Install base packages
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name: "{{ item }}"
        state: present
      with_items:
      - curl
      - ca-certificates
      - python3-venv
      - libpq-dev
      - acl   # needed for become_user to unprivileged users
      tags:
        - packages

  roles:
    - role: geerlingguy.ntp
      tags: ntp
    - { role: common, tags: ["common", "baseline"] }
    - role: nginx
      vars:
        nginx_worker_processes: auto
        nginx_client_max_body_size: 25m
      tags: [nginx, web]

  tasks:
    - name: Create application users
      ansible.builtin.user:
        name: "{{ item.name }}"
        uid: "{{ item.uid }}"
        groups: "{{ item.groups | join(',') }}"
        append: true
        shell: /bin/bash
      loop: "{{ app_users }}"
      loop_control:
        label: "{{ item.name }}"
        index_var: user_idx
        pause: 1
      tags: users

    # sshd hardening; the validate step keeps us from locking ourselves out
    - name: Disable root login over SSH
      ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
        path: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
        regexp: '^#?\s*PermitRootLogin\s+\w+'
        line: 'PermitRootLogin no'
        validate: '/usr/sbin/sshd -t -f %s'
        backup: true
      notify: restart sshd
      tags: [security, ssh]

    - name: Raise listen backlog
      ansible.builtin.lineinfile:
        path: /etc/sysctl.d/60-ledger.conf
        regexp: '^net\.core\.somaxconn\s*='
        line: "net.core.somaxconn = 4096"
        create: true
        mode: "0644"
      when:
        - ansible_virtualization_type != "docker"
        - not (skip_sysctl | default(false) | bool)
        - ansible_kernel is version('5.4', '>=')

    - name: Render nginx vhost
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: templates/nginx/ledger.conf.j2
        dest: "/etc/nginx/sites-available/{{ app_name }}.conf"
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0644"
      notify:
        - validate nginx config
        - reload nginx
      tags: [nginx, deploy]

    - name: Deploy release {{ app_version }}
      tags: deploy
      block:
        - name: Fetch release tarball
          ansible.builtin.get_url:
            url: "https://artifacts.example.internal/ledger/ledger-{{ app_version }}.tar.gz"
            dest: "/tmp/ledger-{{ app_version }}.tar.gz"
            checksum: "sha256:{{ app_sha256 }}"
            mode: "0640"

        - name: Run database migrations
          ansible.builtin.shell: >
            cd {{ release_dir }} &&
            ./venv/bin/python manage.py migrate --noinput
            --database default
            2>&1 | tee -a /var/log/{{ app_name }}/migrate.log
          args:
            executable: /bin/bash
          become_user: "{{ app_user }}"
          register: migrate_out
          changed_when: "'No migrations to apply' not in migrate_out.stdout"
          run_once: true

        - name: Check config with ledger-ctl
          ansible.builtin.command: |
            {{ release_dir }}/venv/bin/ledger-ctl
              --config /etc/ledger/ledger.yml
              check --strict
          changed_when: false

        - name: Point current at the new release
          ansible.builtin.file:
            src: "{{ release_dir }}"
            dest: "{{ app_root }}/current"
            state: link
            force: true
          notify: restart ledger

        - name: Flush handlers before health check
          ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers

        - name: Wait for health endpoint
          ansible.builtin.uri:
            url: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ app_port }}/healthz"
            status_code: 200
            return_content: true
          register: health
          until: health.status == 200 and 'ok' in health.content
          retries:   30
          delay:  5
      rescue:
        - name: Roll back to previous release
          ansible.builtin.file:
            src: "{{ previous_release | default(app_root + '/releases/previous') }}"
            dest: "{{ app_root }}/current"
            state: link
            force: true
          notify: restart ledger
        - name: Fail loudly
          ansible.builtin.fail:
            msg: "Deploy of {{ app_version }} failed on {{ inventory_hostname }}; rolled back."
      always:
        - name: Remove downloaded tarball
          ansible.builtin.file:
            path: "/tmp/ledger-{{ app_version }}.tar.gz"
            state: absent

  handlers:
    - name: restart sshd
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: ssh
        state: restarted
    - name: validate nginx config
      ansible.builtin.command: nginx -t
      changed_when: false
    - name: reload nginx
      ansible.builtin.service:
        name: nginx
        state: reloaded
    - name: restart ledger
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: "ledger@{{ app_port }}"
        state: restarted
        daemon_reload: true

  gather_facts: false
  vars:

    - name: Validate inputs before touching anything

        that:
          - app_version is defined
          - app_version is match('^v?\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-[0-9A-Za-z.]+)?$')
          - deploy_env in ['staging', 'production']
          - "'api' in group_names or 'web' in group_names"
          - (api_workers | default(4) | int) <= 32
        fail_msg: "Refusing to deploy {{ app_version }} to {{ inventory_hostname }} (env={{ deploy_env | default('unset') }})"

      delegate_to: localhost

        url: "{{ release_tracker_url }}/deployments"

          release_id: "{{ release_id }}"
          environment: "{{ deploy_env }}"
          hosts: "{{ ansible_play_hosts_all }}"
          strategy:
            type: rolling
            batch_size: 1
            canary: "{{ groups['canary'] | default([]) }}"
          notify_channels: ["#deploys", "#api-oncall"]
          dry_run: false
        status_code: [200, 201, 202]
        return_content: true
        timeout: 15
      register: deployment
      delegate_to: localhost
      run_once: true

    - name: Remember deployment id
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        deployment_id: "{{ deployment.json.id }}"

    # haproxy runtime API; drain first so in-flight requests can finish
    - name: Drain node on every load balancer

        host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
        backend: ledger_api

        url: "http://{{ ansible_host }}:8080{{ health_path }}"
        return_content: true
      register: health
      until: health.json is defined and health.json.status == 'pass'
      retries:   20
      delay: "{{ drain_seconds | int // 4 }}"

        backend: ledger_api

      run_once: true

  handlers:
    - name: restart ledger-api

        name: ledger-api
        state: restarted
      become: true

name: Release

on:
  push:

concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
  VERSION:   ${{ inputs.version || github.ref_name }}

  build:
    name: Build dist (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-22.04, macos-14, windows-2022]
    steps:

        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

        with:
          output-dir: dist
      - name: Build sdist
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: pipx run build --sdist --outdir dist
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: dist-${{ matrix.os }}
          path: |
            dist/*.whl
            dist/*.tar.gz
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  container:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 45
    outputs:
      digest: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@v3
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:

        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_TYPE:  INCOMING_WEBHOOK@@SP@@
